# Staging `ces-revisions`: outcomes and tracks to rank

Nothing is built yet: the package is a greeting and two smoke tests. There is no spec, only the brief and three research files, so this is the new-project entry. Before I write any roadmap text, I need you to rank the outcomes below and confirm the tracks.

Every outcome below is a **candidate**. Each is drawn from the brief (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`), since you haven't stated outcomes in your own words yet. I've read only the openings of the three research files, so they inform the notes below but add no outcomes.

The literature review and gap analysis (Parts A and B of the brief) already exist as those three files, so I haven't staged them. Say so if you want a reconciled single synthesis as an outcome.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Track | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A vintage table of total nonfarm monthly change: 1st, 2nd and 3rd print, preliminary and final benchmark, SA and NSA | A | Small data: about 4,800 values (about 480 months × 5 stages × SA/NSA). How far back public vintages go is unknown; Stage 1 measures it. |
| O2 | The same table by NAICS supersector | A | About 53k values (×~11 supersectors). Whether supersector vintages are public before recent years is unknown; it may need archived releases built by hand. |
| O3 | Revision **scale** over time for each of the four stages, with 2003 and 2020–22 marked (descriptive, no model) | A | Negligible compute once O1 exists |
| O4 | The effect of collection interval (days from the reference week to first closing) and first-closing rate on the scale of 1- and 2-month revisions | B | About 480 dates built by hand from release calendars. How far back published collection rates go is unknown. |
| O5 | The seasonal-factor versus NSA-sample split of SA 1- and 2-month revisions | C | Needs NSA vintages from O1. Compute unknown until run. |
| O6 | Benchmark error and wedge-back as an irregular, higher-precision observation, with birth-death error varying by supersector | D | Needs O2. About 40 benchmark events per sector. |
| O7 | Agency-capacity covariates (real appropriations, FTE, sample size) and their honestly shrunk effect on revision scale | E | About 40 annual values per covariate, built by hand from budget justifications and FedScope. Mostly your time; size unknown. |
| O8 | A joint four-stage news/noise state-space model (stochastic volatility, Student-t, supersector hierarchy, horseshoe) unifying O4–O7 | F | NUTS compute unknown; its core stage measures it |
| O9 | Validation: targeted posterior predictive checks, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time | F | Pseudo-real-time means many refits; cost is a multiple of O8's fit time |

## Tracks

- **A — Vintage panel (known progression).** Every other track consumes it. Please confirm you can name its stages first to last; if not, it's research.
- **B — Collection interval (research).** Split from the other driver tracks: its answer stands without them, and its within-year variation is the best-identified of the drivers.
- **C — Seasonal versus sample decomposition (research).** Split because it answers *where* SA revision comes from, which stands without any driver effect.
- **D — Benchmark and birth-death (research).** Split because it concerns a different revision stage with a different data cadence.
- **E — Agency capacity (research).** Split because it is a slow-moving, collinear, weakly identified question. Joined with B, B would wait on hand-built budget data.
- **F — Joint model and validation (research).** It depends on whichever of B–E you want unified. You may instead want F to *be* the project, with B–E as its components; tell me which.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 and uv, from the repo.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ and Polars, from the brief. Please confirm. A cheap check worth running is whether JAX has 3.14 wheels.

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. That file doesn't exist yet.

## One optional probe

I could fetch one real vintage listing, ALFRED's PAYEMS release dates, to firm up the O1 and O2 coverage notes. I'll only do this if you say yes.

## What I need from you

Please do these in one reply:

1. Rank the outcomes within each track.
2. Rank the tracks among themselves.
3. Confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (including A as known progression and F's role), and the name.
